title: The checkerboard
text: Close to a fifth of McKinley County is Navajo Nation off-reservation trust land, as of 2024. Across the eastern Navajo region, land became a checkerboard, with Navajo allotments and tribal trust land scattered among private, railroad, and state holdings. The Eastern Navajo Agency checkerboard is distinct from the rest of the reservation, even in which federal programs control it.

s2.title: Land Base Formation, Navajo Nation
s2.publisher: Diné Nihi Kéyah Project (Indian Country Grassroots)
s2.quote: Like other reservations, huge swathes of the eastern Navajo reservation became isolated checkerboards of allotments, tribal trust, private, railroad and state lands. ... The Eastern Navajo Agency checkerboard is distinct from the rest of the reservation in character of land and isolation, and even by which federal program controls it.
